ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left of the figure is a benzene ring, and two adjacent positions of the benzene ring are substituted; one ortho substituent is an acyl fragment connected to the benzene ring, and the carbonyl carbon is further connected to a carbon chain bearing R1; the other ortho substituent is N-H. This nitrogen is connected to the right to an enolate/enamine-like C=C fragment: R2 is attached to the upper alkene carbon away from nitrogen, and the negatively charged O− is attached to the lower alkene carbon connected to nitrogen, so O− and N are at substituent positions on the same alkene carbon. The curved arrows in the figure are ignored according to the problem statement. Reasoning: R1 and R2 are represented by the wildcard *. The acyl side chain is written as benzene ring-C(=O)C*. Nitrogen is connected to the ortho position of the benzene ring, so the aromatic ring part can be written as Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*. In the right enolate fragment, the R2 wildcard is on the distal alkene carbon, and N and [O-] are on the other alkene carbon, and it is encoded according to the depicted double-bond geometry as */C=C(\[O-])N. Connect this fragment with the ortho-substituted benzene ring to obtain the SMILES: */C=C(\[O-])Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a skeletal structure, ignoring the curved arrows: an ortho-disubstituted benzene has an acyl side chain on one ring carbon and an N-H substituent on the adjacent ring carbon. The acyl side is written as c1...C(=O)C* to represent the carbonyl attached to the ring and a terminal carbon bearing R1. The N substituent connects to an alkene/enolate fragment bearing R2 and O−, written as */C=C(\[O-])N when the drawn alkene geometry is encoded. Then attach the nitrogen to the adjacent aromatic ring atom and complete the benzene as Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*, yielding */C=C(\[O-])Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧是一个苯环，苯环相邻的两个位置被取代；一个邻位取代基是与苯环相连的酰基片段 C(=O)-C(R1)，另一个邻位取代基是一个 N-H。该氮再连接到右侧的烯醇盐/烯胺样片段：N 连到一个 C=C 片段，另一端烯碳连有 R2 和带负电的氧 O−。图中的弯箭头按题意忽略。推理：R1 和 R2 用通配符 * 表示。酰基侧链写作苯环-C(=O)C*。氮连接到邻位苯环，因此芳环部分可写为 Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*。右侧烯醇盐片段按图示双键几何编码为 */C=C(\[O-])N。将该片段与邻位取代苯环相连，得到 SMILES：*/C=C(\[O-])Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*。

method.CoT_qualify_0: Revise the image description of the enolate/alkene fragment. The image shows R2 attached to the distal/upper alkene carbon, while O− is attached to the N-bearing/lower alkene carbon; they are not both on the same “other end” alkene carbon. Keep the final SMILES as */C=C(\[O-])Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*, which correctly places [O-] and N on the same alkene carbon and R2 as the wildcard on the other alkene carbon. The trace otherwise follows the required order of first describing the image and then reasoning.
method.CoT_after_polish_1: 图像描述：图中左侧是一个苯环，苯环相邻的两个位置被取代；一个邻位取代基是与苯环相连的酰基片段，羰基碳再连到带 R1 的碳链；另一个邻位取代基是 N-H。该氮向右连接到一个烯醇盐/烯胺样的 C=C 片段：R2 连在远离氮的上方烯碳上，带负电的 O− 连在与氮相连的下方烯碳上，因此 O− 与 N 位于同一个烯碳的取代位置。图中的弯箭头按题意忽略。推理：R1 和 R2 用通配符 * 表示。酰基侧链写作苯环-C(=O)C*。氮连接到苯环邻位，因此芳环部分可写为 Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*。右侧烯醇盐片段中，R2 通配符在远端烯碳，N 和 [O-] 在另一烯碳，并按图示双键几何编码为 */C=C(\[O-])N。将该片段与邻位取代苯环相连，得到 SMILES：*/C=C(\[O-])Nc1ccccc1C(=O)C*。
method.CoT_qualify_1: Trace is acceptable. It first describes the image and then reasons, ignores the curved arrows as instructed, represents R1/R2 as wildcards, identifies the ortho-disubstituted benzene, acyl substituent, N-H substituent, enolate/alkene fragment, and produces a SMILES consistent with the standard answer. Minor note: wording could say the benzene is lower-left rather than simply left, but this does not affect correctness.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct graph-to-SMILES transcription from the drawn skeletal formula; no reaction-mechanism interpretation is needed beyond ignoring the curved arrows and treating R1/R2 as unspecified substituent wildcards.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the actual molecular graph: a benzene ring with adjacent substituents; one substituent is an acyl group C(=O)C* where the terminal carbon bears R1, and the other is an anilino N-H attached to an enolate/alkene fragment with R2 as a wildcard, C=C([O-])N. Also read the alkene geometry from the drawn relative positions and ignore all curved arrows.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction to output a SMILES expression for the transition-state structure and to ignore the arrows, so curved arrows are not translated into bonds or charges.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard SMILES conventions: aromatic benzene as c1ccccc1, bracketed charged oxygen as [O-], unspecified R groups as *, carbonyl as C(=O), amine nitrogen as N, and / or \ to encode the drawn alkene stereochemistry. Combine substituents on adjacent aromatic atoms into a single connected SMILES.
